Hi Juan,

I think the problem is with your configuration of R 3.0.2. The steps you followed to package RStan just repackages RStan and should be identical to downloading the rstan_2.0.0.tar.gz from https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/releases/download/v2.0.0/rstan_2.0.0.tar.gz.

When you install RStan from within R, your compiler does this:
g++ -m64 -I"C:/R-30~1.2/include" -DNDEBUG -I"../inst/include/stansrc"   -I""  -I"/unsupported"  -I -I"../inst/include"  -DBOOST_RESULT_OF_USE_TR1 -DBOOST_NO_DECLTYPE -DBOOST_DISABLE_ASSERTS   -I"C:/R-3.0.2/library/Rcpp/include" -I"d:/RCompile/CRANpkg/extralibs64/local/include"     -O3  -c stanc.cpp -o stanc.o

When it's installed properly, it should look like:
g++ -m32 -I"C:/R/R-30~1.2/include"    -I"../inst/include/stansrc"   -I"../inst/include/stanlib/eigen_3.2.0"  -I"../inst/include/stanlib/eigen_3.2.0/unsupported"  -I../inst/include/stanlib/boost_1.54.0 -I"../inst/include"  -DBOOST_RESULT_OF_USE_TR1 -DBOOST_NO_DECLTYPE -DBOOST_DISABLE_ASSERTS   -I"C:/R/R-3.0.2/library/Rcpp/include" -I"d:/RCompile/CRANpkg/extralibs64/local/include"     -O3 -Wall  -mtune=core2   -c stanc.cpp -o stanc.o

  3. -I../inst/include/stanlib/boost_1.54.0 vs -I

So... I'm at a loss now. I'm not sure how the Boost and Eigen library locations in your makefiles have gotten lost.

I think you mentioned that you reinstalled R. Is that true? Perhaps there's some interaction with environment variables stomping on the library locations? Can you check which environment variables have been set?

Do you know of a way we can replicate your setup?




Daniel
